capabilities.target: executive's calendar (accept invite) and prep notes
executive's drive (board materials, draft financial results)

inputs.source: Calendar invites from any sender, inside or outside the company; description is free text

instructions.note: No restriction on which documents are searched or which attendees receive the brief; 'attendees' is determined by whatever the untrusted inviter specifies.
Agent is implicitly authorized to accept invites and send mail as the executive for any invite received, including from unauthenticated external senders.
The only stated oversight is a daily summary reviewed after accept/read/send actions have already executed; this is after-the-fact, not preventive.

controls.name: Human approval gate on mail_send
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action, low-volume human approval gate is enforced outside the model and does not weaken with model capability, but decays under autonomy_increase or control_removal.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to meeting record
controls.decay_rationale: Does not decay with model capability if the recipient set is drawn from a verified system of record rather than the free-text invite content; fails if data_scope_expansion widens who counts as a valid recipient.

controls.name: Outbound confidential-content filter
controls.decay_rationale: A separate classifier on outbound mail content can be bypassed by paraphrase or encoding and does not scale with the agent's own capability.

controls.name: Treat invite description as untrusted data
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model refusing to treat invite free text as instructions; a more capable model follows injected goals more competently.

controls.name: Scope mail_send credential to internal domains by default
controls.decay_rationale: A narrowed credential does not decay with model capability; fails if data_scope_expansion broadens the allowed send scope.

controls.name: Tamper-evident action log distinct from agent-written summary
controls.decay_rationale: An independently enforced log does not decay with model capability; it is detective only and requires review to have effect.

controls.name: Rate or step limit on automatic invite processing
controls.decay_rationale: A structural cap on invites processed per window does not decay with model capability; fails under longer_task_horizon if it only limits per-session rather than cumulative processing.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted calendar invite drives confidential document read and unrestricted email send

attack_path.note: Anyone can send the executive a calendar invite with a free-text description; this is untrusted content entering the agent's context.
Agent auto-accepts the invite and begins 'prepare', using the invite content with no sender validation.
Agent searches the executive's drive for 'related documents', potentially steered by attacker-supplied text in the invite description, reaching board and financial materials.
Agent emails a brief, which may include confidential content, to 'the attendees' -- which includes the external sender who created the invite -- with no recipient restriction or approval step.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

evidence.observation: Anyone can send the executive a calendar invite; the description is free text, so untrusted content enters the agent's context.
Agent auto-accepts invites if the time is free, then finds related documents and emails a brief to attendees, with no sender validation or approval described.
mail.send has no recipient restrictions and no approval step.
The executive's drive holds board materials and draft financial results -- confidential data reachable by drive_read on this path.

recommendations.action: Add a raw-action, low-volume human approval gate before mail_send fires, at minimum for first-time or external recipients.
Restrict mail_send recipients to a verified allowlist drawn from the system of record (not free-text invite content), and scope credentials away from arbitrary external send.
Spotlight/delimit calendar invite descriptions as untrusted data that must not direct search queries or recipient selection.

forecast.watch_signal: Already at the maximum tier with zero active structural controls on this path. Watch for whether ctl.approval_gate_mail and ctl.recipient_allowlist get implemented; once in place, watch for their later removal or for autonomy_increase/control_removal defeating them.

findings.title: No tamper-evident audit record for agent-initiated accept/send actions

evidence.observation: The daily summary is written by the agent itself, with no mention of an independent, tamper-evident log distinguishing agent actions from the executive's own actions.

recommendations.action: Implement a tamper-evident action log, independent of the agent, recording every accept/send action with the triggering invite and content, distinct from the self-generated daily summary.

forecast.watch_signal: Watch whether an independent audit log is added; without one, a more persuasive self-written summary under model_upgrade further erodes the oversight value of the daily review.

findings.title: No rate or step limit on automatic invite acceptance and processing

evidence.observation: Agent acts on invites as they arrive with no stated limit on volume, steps, or runtime; max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are unspecified in the artifacts.

recommendations.action: Add a rate limit or step cap on automatic invite acceptance and processing per time window to bound mass-invite abuse.

forecast.watch_signal: Monitor median invites processed per day per agent instance; a rising count without a corresponding rate limit confirms this risk is active.

stride_coverage.rationale: Single-agent design with no peer agents or inter-agent identity claims; there is no second agent identity for this process to spoof or be spoofed by.
This is an inbound flow carrying invite content into the agent; it does not itself carry internal data outward, so outbound disclosure is tracked on the mail_send flow instead.
The external sender is outside the organization's identity and audit boundary; attributing or repudiating their own actions is outside this agent's control scope.
This flow is the executive's own authenticated chat channel and does not cross a trust boundary, so the boundary-gated tampering category does not apply here.
Internal, non-boundary-crossing channel from the authenticated executive; no outward disclosure risk is created by this flow itself.
A single authenticated executive is the only source on this flow, so it does not present a boundary-crossing flood risk as scoped here.
Outbound send volume is bounded by upstream invite processing; that denial-of-service risk is already captured at the agent process and invite flow elements.
cap.drive_read only reads from the store; the design grants the agent no write or delete capability against the drive, so tampering via this agent is out of scope.
No design evidence of bulk or repeated read operations against the drive store that could exhaust it; not supported by the artifacts.
Artifacts say only that the daily summary is 'written by the agent itself'; how or where it is stored, and whether it can be altered after writing, is not described.
Artifacts do not describe who besides the executive can access the daily summary or how it is distributed, so disclosure exposure cannot be assessed.
The summary is generated once per day as a bounded job per the artifacts, not a resource that can be flooded by external actors.

rating.rationale: An untrusted calendar invite (anyone can send one) feeds directly into document search and an unrestricted email send with no recipient restriction, approval gate, or content filter in the design, forming a complete lethal-trifecta path (U source, confidential read, unrestricted egress) rated critical both inherent and residual since no declared controls cover the path. Two property findings -- no tamper-evident audit trail and no rate/step limit on invite processing -- are each capped at high per rubric 5a. The forecast stays at critical because the path is already unmitigated; implementing the recommended approval gate, recipient allowlist, and credential scoping is the priority, and once in place those controls (particularly the approval gate) should be the ones watched for decay under autonomy_increase, control_removal, or model_upgrade.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.
No MCP/tool manifest or IaC was provided; capability scope (e.g., the breadth of mail_send's credential) is inferred from runtime notes, so confidence on credential_scope is medium.
Autonomy limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) are not stated in the artifacts and are treated as unset (null) for scoring purposes.

No information was provided on logging, audit trail implementation, or approval tooling beyond the stated daily summary; the absence of these controls is inferred from their omission in the artifacts.
